card.title: 4e BRIGADE
card.text: Deployment: Gets +1 attack for each non-French unit you control.
card.flavorText: The 4th Brigade was part of the 1st Free French Division, one of the principal units of the Free French Forces (FFL) during WW2. It was formed in London by men who decided to keep fighting after the fall of France, and it consisted of personnel from both France and its colonies. They were the first to join the FFL and participated in numerous battles and campaigns against the Axis forces in Africa, Middle East, Italy and France, and became the most decorated French division of WW2 alongside the 3rd Algerian Infantry Division. The division most notably distinguished itself during the Battle of Bir Hakeim which took place in an oasis in the Libyan desert south and west of Tobruk, between May 26 and June 11, 1942. During the battle, Général de brigade Marie-Pierre Kœnig and 3,700 his men defended the position against Panzerarmee Afrika commanded by General Erwin Rommel, a ten times larger force. The delay imposed on the Axis offensive by the defense of Bir Hakeim influenced the cancellation of Operation Herkules, the Axis invasion of Malta, and allowed the British forces, to retreat, regroup and prepare for the following confrontation, the First Battle of Alamein, which would be a decisive victory for the Allies.  Later, in 1944, the 1st Free French Division was part of the Italian campaign and the Allied landing in Provence. They fought their way through German defenses on the French territory, until they reached Alsace and liberated Colmar. They ended the war crossing the Italian border in the Alps.
